key_insight: EndoCoT embeds an internal, evolving chain-of-thought inside the diffusion denoising loop so an MLLM provides stepwise, adaptive guidance rather than a single static encoding, enabling deeper multimodal reasoning.
problem_solved: Fixes two limitations of current MLLM+diffusion pipelines: shallow single-step encoding that fails to trigger chain-of-thought, and guidance that remains invariant across denoising steps, reducing accuracy on complex tasks like spatial reasoning.
method: Endogenous Chain-of-Thought: generate intermediate reasoning tokens inside the diffusion denoising process so the model reasons and updates guidance at each step.
Tight coupling & lightweight adapters: integrate the MLLM and diffusion denoiser with stepwise conditioning and feedback so reasoning evolves without expensive external prompting.
Training objectives for stability: use consistency and curriculum-style losses to scale CoT depth while keeping compute and memory efficient.
impact: Makes diffusion-based multimodal models substantially better at complex, interpretable reasoning tasks by providing adaptive, stepwise guidance — improving accuracy and explainability for practitioners building spatial, planning, or multi-step vision–language applications.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: diffusion denoising loop with internal CoT tokens generated and fed back each step (highlight evolving guidance).
Before vs After chart: task accuracy / reasoning depth for standard single-step encoder vs EndoCoT.
Stepwise example: a spatial-reasoning example showing intermediate CoT states and how they change the generated image/answer.
Icon set: MLLM encoder, CoT token stream, diffusion timesteps, and a final output/checkmark to denote improved correctness.
paper_title: EndoCoT: Scaling Endogenous Chain-of-Thought Reasoning in Diffusion Models
paper_authors: Xuanlang Dai, Yujie Zhou, Long Xing, Jiazi Bu, Xilin Wei
